docs.title: HoopsLab
docs.text:
Track the full game live. Print the halftime report in seconds. One tool for coaches who need instant intelligence — not post-game spreadsheets.

<1s PDF render 100% Game-day flow 1 tool Track → Share 🎥 Live Command Center

Real-time event logging with shot clock, quarter timer, player subs, and play tagging. Halftime-ready summaries in seconds.

📊 Automatic Intelligence

TS%, eFG%, Net Rating, lineup impact, duo/trio matrices, and shot quality models — calculated instantly from your tracking data.

📄 Print & Share

Server-side PDF reports for games, players, lineups, seasons, and clutch situations. Export as ZIP bundles or email to players.

🎯 Shot Charts & Heatmaps

Court-mapped shot locations with hexbin heatmaps and zone efficiency analysis. See hot and cold areas at a glance.

👥 Lineup Analytics

On/off court splits, duo/trio compatibility, 5-man unit rankings, and rotation analysis. Know who works with whom.

📋 Digital Playbook

65+ pre-loaded plays with a visual diagram builder. Track play effectiveness with points-per-possession analysis.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: HoopsLab provides JSON API endpoints for programmatic access to games, players, analytics, and playbook data.

docs.title: Base URLs
docs.text:
Environment URL Local dev http://localhost:8080 Production https://your-domain.com

All API routes that don't start with /api/ render HTML pages.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Most API endpoints require authentication via Flask-Login session cookie.

For programmatic access, use the login endpoint first:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/auth/login \
  -d "username=admin&password=admin123" \
  -c cookies.txt

Then include the cookie in subsequent requests:

curl http://localhost:8080/api/v1/plays -b cookies.txt

docs.title: Rust Module (PyO3)

The basketball_stats_rust package provides compiled performance-critical functions:

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: Guide for deploying HoopsLab to production environments.

docs.title: Options Overview
docs.text: Method Best For Difficulty Docker Compose Servers, NAS, single-machine Easy Docker + Registry Kubernetes, multi-host Medium Manual VPS, custom setup Medium

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker & Docker Compose installed
  • Git

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
# 1. Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/GiulioMastromartino/Basketball-stats.git
cd Basketball-stats

# 2. Configure environment
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env with your settings

# 3. Start the stack
docker-compose up -d

This starts:

Service Purpose db PostgreSQL 16 with persistent volume web Flask app via Gunicorn on port 8080 cloudflared Optional Cloudflare Tunnel for public HTTPS access

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Set these in .env or in docker-compose.override.yml:

Variable Required Default Description SECRET_KEY Yes — Flask session signing key (generate a random string) DATABASE_URL No SQLite postgresql://user:pass@db/basketball_stats FLASK_ENV No development Set to production for production DISABLE_AUTH No false true for single-user/personal deployments CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN No — For Cloudflare Tunnel public access

docs.title: Building & Publishing the Image
docs.text:
# Build the multi-stage image (Rust + Python)
docker build -t your-registry/basketball-stats:latest .

# Push to registry
docker push your-registry/basketball-stats:latest

The multi-stage build: 1. Stage 1 (Rust Builder) — Compiles the Rust analytics module via PyO3/maturin 2. Stage 2 (Final) — Installs Python deps + the compiled Rust wheel

docs.title: TrueNAS Scale Deployment
docs.text:
1. Go to Apps → Discover Apps → Custom App
  2. Application Name: basketball-stats
  3. Image: your-registry/basketball-stats:latest
  4. Environment Variables:
  5. DATABASE_URL: sqlite:////app/data/basketball_stats.db
  6. SECRET_KEY: (generate a random string)
  7. FLASK_ENV: production
  8. Storage: Map persistent host paths:
  9. /mnt/pool/app-data → /app/instance (database)
  10. /mnt/pool/games → /app/Games (CSV import)
  11. /mnt/pool/output → /app/Output (generated files)
  12. Networking: Container port 8080 → Node port 9080

docs.title: Analytics & Reports
docs.text: Advanced analytics engine providing deep insights into player performance, lineup efficiency, shot quality, and clutch performance.

docs.title: Analytics Dashboard
docs.text: Access the analytics dashboard at /analytics after logging in.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text: Tab Description Team Overview Season summary, top performers, scoring trends Player Comparison Select 2+ players to compare stats side-by-side Progression Per-game stat trends for individual players Consistency Leaderboard ranked by consistency index Shooting Shooting efficiency breakdown by player and zone Roles Player role classification based on statistical profile

docs.title: True Shooting % (TS%)
docs.text:
Measures shooting efficiency accounting for field goals, 3-pointers, and free throws.

TS% = PTS / (2 × (FGA + 0.44 × FTA))
Range Rating 60%+ Excellent 55–60% Good 50–55% Average <50% Below average

docs.title: Effective FG% (eFG%)
docs.text:
Adjusts FG% for the fact that 3-pointers are worth more than 2-pointers.

eFG% = (FGM + 0.5 × 3PM) / FGA

docs.title: True Usage Rate (USG%)
docs.text:
Percentage of team plays used by a player while on the court.

USG% = ((FGA + 0.44 × FTA + TOV) × (Team Minutes / 5)) / (Minutes × Team Possessions) × 100
Range Role 20%+ High usage (primary scorer) 15–20% Average usage <15% Low usage (role player)

docs.title: Points Per Shot (PPS)
docs.text:
Simple efficiency metric measuring points scored per field goal attempt.

PPS = Points / FGA
Range Rating 1.10+ Excellent 1.00–1.10 Good <1.00 Below average

docs.title: Game Score
docs.text:
Holistic measure of a player's single-game productivity (similar to NBA's Game Score).

Game Score = PTS + 0.4 × FG - 0.7 × FGA - 0.4 × (FTA - FT) + 0.7 × OREB + 0.3 × DREB
             + STL + 0.7 × AST + 0.7 × BLK - 0.4 × PF - TOV

docs.title: Net Rating
docs.text:
Points scored minus points allowed per 100 possessions.

Net Rating = ORtg - DRtg
Range Impact +15+ Elite impact +5 to +15 Positive impact -5 to +5 Neutral < -5 Negative impact

docs.title: Shot Quality Model
docs.text:
Assigns expected point values to different court zones. Calculated in Rust via PyO3 for performance.

Zone Expected Value Rim 1.20 pts Paint (non-rim) 0.85 pts Midrange 0.75 pts Corner 3 1.10 pts Above Break 3 1.05 pts Free Throw 0.75 pts

docs.title: Shot Quality Delta
docs.text:
Shot Quality Delta = Actual Points - Expected Points
  • Positive = "Tough shot maker" (outperforming expectations)
  • Negative = "Poor shot selection" (underperforming expectations)

docs.title: On/Off Court Splits
docs.text:
Compare team performance when a player is on vs off the court:

Metric Description ORtg Points scored per 100 possessions DRtg Points allowed per 100 possessions Net Rating ORtg - DRtg Net Differential On Court Net - Off Court Net

Positive differential = player has a positive impact on team performance.

docs.title: Duo Compatibility
docs.text:
Shows how two-player combinations perform together:

  • Synergy Factor — Combined net rating when both players are on court
  • Compatibility Matrix — Color-coded grid (green = positive, red = negative)

docs.title: Trio Combinations
docs.text: Three-player lineup combinations ranked by net rating.

docs.title: 5-Man Lineup Rankings
docs.text: Full 5-man units ranked by Net Rating with minimum possession threshold.

docs.title: Rotation Analysis
docs.text: Visualize substitution patterns and player minute distributions across a game.

docs.title: Court Mapping
docs.text: Shots plotted using x_loc and y_loc coordinates: - Court dimensions: 0–500 (x), 0–470 (y) - Basket located at (250, 50)

docs.title: Visualization Types
docs.text: Type Description Shot Markers Individual makes (green) and misses (red) Hexbin Heatmap Grouped by zone with FG% coloring Zone Efficiency Aggregated stats by court zone

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text: Filter shot charts by: - Player — View individual shot profiles - Game Type — Season, Friendly, or Playoff - Play Type — Shots from specific plays (e.g., "Pick & Roll")

docs.title: Four Factors (Dean Oliver)
docs.text:
Factor Weight Description Effective FG% 40% Shooting efficiency (eFG%) Turnover % 25% Turnovers per possession Offensive Rebound % 20% OREB rate Free Throw Rate 15% FTA / FGA

Each factor is displayed with your team's value vs. opponent value and a composite score.

docs.title: Clutch Performance
docs.text:
Stats filtered for "Crunch Time" situations: - Score within 5 points - Less than 5 minutes remaining in the 4th quarter or overtime

Available views: - Player Clutch Stats — Individual performance in clutch situations - Team Clutch Summary — Aggregate clutch performance - Clutch Leaders — Top performers ranked by clutch points

The fastest path to a running app with sample data:

1 Clone the repo 
git clone https://github.com/GiulioMastromartino/Basketball-stats.git
cd Basketball-stats
2 Create & activate a virtual environment 
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate   # macOS/Linux
venv\Scripts\activate      # Windows
3 Install dependencies 
pip install -r requirements-local.txt

This installs Flask, SQLAlchemy, Pandas, WeasyPrint, and all other dependencies.

4 Run the app 
python quick_start.py

This single command:

  • Creates the SQLite database
  • Creates an admin user & default team
  • Seeds 3 sample games with player stats
  • Starts the dev server on http://localhost:8080
5 Log in

Open http://localhost:8080 and log in with:

Usernameadmin Passwordadmin123

What you'll see

After logging in you'll see the Dashboard with 3 sample games (Lakers win, Warriors loss, Celtics win) and summary metrics. Click any game to explore the full detail page with box scores, shot charts, and advanced stats.

docs.title: Local Setup (Step by Step)
docs.text: Use this when you want full control over the setup process.

docs.title: 1. Clone & Enter
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/GiulioMastromartino/Basketball-stats.git
cd Basketball-stats

docs.title: 2. Virtual Environment
docs.text:
python -m venv venv

# Activate:
# macOS/Linux
source venv/bin/activate

# Windows
venv\Scripts\activate

You should see (venv) in your terminal prompt.

docs.title: 3. Install Dependencies
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements-local.txt

This installs ~20 packages including Flask 3.0, SQLAlchemy 2.0, Pandas, WeasyPrint, and testing tools.

For production deployments use requirements.txt instead (adds gunicorn, psycopg2, WorkOS SSO, Prometheus metrics).

docs.title: 4. Database Setup
docs.text:
Create all tables and seed initial data:

# Option A: Quick start (creates DB + sample data + starts server)
python quick_start.py --no-run

# Option B: Manual with Flask CLI
export FLASK_APP=manage.py
flask shell -c "from web import create_app; app=create_app(); app.app_context().push(); from core.models import db; db.create_all()"

docs.title: 5. Import Your Data
docs.text:
Place CSV files in the Games/ directory, then:

python -c "from cli_import import main; main()"

Or use the web UI: navigate to Upload Game in the sidebar.

docs.title: 6. Run the Server
docs.text:
python quick_start.py

Or for more control:

python run.py --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --env development

docs.title: Docker Setup
docs.text: For server deployments, NAS (TrueNAS Scale), or cleaner isolation.

docs.title: Using Docker Compose (Recommended)
docs.text:
docker-compose up -d

This starts three services:

Service Purpose db PostgreSQL 16 (persistent storage) web Flask app with Gunicorn on port 8080 cloudflared Optional Cloudflare Tunnel for public access

The app will be available at http://localhost:8080.

docs.title: Building the Image Manually
docs.text:
# Build
docker build -t your-username/basketball-stats:latest .

# Push to registry
docker push your-username/basketball-stats:latest

# Run
docker run -d \
  -p 8080:8080 \
  -e SECRET_KEY="your-secret-key" \
  -v ./instance:/app/instance \
  your-username/basketball-stats:latest

docs.title: TrueNAS Scale Deployment
docs.text:
1. Go to Apps → Discover Apps → Custom App
  2. Application Name: basketball-stats
  3. Image: your-username/basketball-stats:latest
  4. Environment Variables:
    • DATABASE_URL: sqlite:////app/data/basketball_stats.db
    • SECRET_KEY: (generate a random string)
  5. Storage: Map host paths to /app/data, /app/Games, /app/Output
  6. Networking: Container port 8080 → Node port 9080

docs.title: First Steps After Login
docs.text:
Once you're logged in, here's what to do first:

1 Explore the Dashboard

Your dashboard shows recent games with win/loss highlighting, summary metrics (Total Games, Active Players, Record, Win Rate), and a list of all games. Click any game card to dive into details.

2 Check the Players Page

Browse player cards showing PPG, RPG, APG, EFF, ORtg, PPP, TS%, and USG%. Switch to Table View for all 28+ advanced metrics with color-coded performance indicators.

3 View a Game Detail

Click any game to see the full breakdown: Box Score, Advanced Stats, Shot Chart, Plays Analysis, and Lineup Combinations. Download PDF reports from the action bar.

4 Try Live Game Tracking

Click Live Game in the sidebar to start tracking a game in real-time — shot locations, quarter timer, player substitutions, play tagging, and +/- tracking.

5 Generate PDF Reports

Every game, player, and team page has an Export PDF button. Try the Visual Game Report, Player Scouting Card, or Clutch Time Report.

docs.title: CSV Format
docs.text:
Filename pattern: 

Opponent_YourScore-TheirScore_DD-MM-YYYY_Type.csv

Examples:

File Game Type Lakers_105-98_15-03-2024_S.csv Season Warriors_88-92_20-03-2024_P.csv Playoff Celtics_95-90_25-03-2024_F.csv Friendly

Required columns: 

Name, MIN, PTS, FGM, FGA, FG%, 3PM, 3PA, 3P%,
FTM, FTA, FT%, OREB, DREB, REB, AST, TOV, STL, BLK, PF

Import: 

# Place your CSV files in the Games/ folder, then:
python -c "from cli_import import main; main()"

docs.title: PDF & JSON Import
docs.text: You can also upload PDF game reports (parsed automatically) or JSON exports directly through the web UI at Upload Game in the sidebar.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Key environment variables you can set in .env:

Variable Default Description SECRET_KEY auto-generated Flask session signing key DATABASE_URL sqlite:///basketball_stats.db Database connection string FLASK_ENV development development, testing, or production DISABLE_AUTH false Set to true for single-user setups GAMES_DIR ./Games Directory for CSV import files OUTPUT_DIR ./Output Directory for generated outputs LOG_LEVEL INFO Logging verbosity MAIL_SERVER smtp.gmail.com SMTP server for email reports

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution Port 8080 already in use python quick_start.py --port 8081 or python run.py --port 8081 Database errors python quick_start.py --reset to reset and recreate Module not found Make sure your virtual environment is activated and pip install -r requirements-local.txt completed CSV import fails Check filename matches pattern exactly, verify all required columns are present PDF generation fails Ensure WeasyPrint is installed correctly — on macOS: brew install pango Docker build fails Ensure Docker has enough memory allocated (minimum 4GB recommended)

docs.title: Live Game Tracking
docs.text: Track basketball games in real-time with shot locations, player substitutions, play tagging, and automatic stat calculations.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Live Game Tracker is a full-screen interface optimized for mobile and tablet use during games. It provides:

  • Shot Clock & Quarter Timer — Keep track of game time
  • Player Substitutions — Manage who's on the court
  • Shot Charting — Record makes and misses on a court diagram
  • Play Tagging — Associate shots with plays from your playbook
  • +/- Tracking — Real-time plus/minus for each player
  • Halftime Summary — Generate PDF reports at halftime
  • Auto-Save — Game state cached in localStorage for crash recovery

docs.title: 1. Access the Live Game Page
docs.text: Click Live Game in the sidebar navigation. The interface opens in fullscreen mode.

docs.title: 2. Set Up Players
docs.text:
Before tracking, ensure your roster is set up:

  • Players are pre-loaded from your team roster
  • Use the substitution panel to set the starting five
  • Bench players appear in a separate list

docs.title: 3. Start the Game
docs.text: Click Start Game to begin tracking. The shot clock and quarter timer start automatically.

docs.title: Recording Shots
docs.text:
1 Select the shooter

Tap the player who took the shot from the active player list.

2 Mark the location

Tap the court diagram where the shot was taken. The system records x/y coordinates automatically.

3 Choose result & play

Select Make or Miss, optionally tag the play from your playbook, and confirm.

docs.title: Substitutions
docs.text:
• Tap Sub next to any active player
  • Select the substitute from the bench
  • The system tracks minutes played automatically

docs.title: Fouls & Turnovers
docs.text: Use the action buttons to record: - Foul — Player commits a foul - Turnover — Player turns over the ball - Timeout — Log a timeout

docs.title: Shot Charting
docs.text:
Shots are plotted on a half-court SVG diagram:

Color Meaning 🟢 Green Made shot 🔴 Red Missed shot Size 2PT vs 3PT (3PT markers are larger)

The system automatically calculates: - Field goal percentage by zone - Heatmap of shot concentration - Points per shot by court area

docs.title: Player +/- Tracking
docs.text:
Each player's plus/minus updates in real-time:

  • +1 when your team scores while they're on court
  • -1 when the opponent scores while they're on court
  • Running totals displayed in the player panel

docs.title: Halftime Summary
docs.text: At halftime, click Halftime PDF to generate a printable report with: - First-half box score - Shooting percentages - Player +/- summary - Possession breakdown

docs.title: End Game
docs.text:
When the game ends, click End Game to: 1. Review the final stats 2. Tag any remaining plays 3. Save the game to the database 4. Generate the final PDF report

The game is then available in the Games list with full detail.

docs.title: Auto-Save & Crash Recovery
docs.text:
The live game state is automatically saved to your browser's localStorage every 30 seconds. If the page is accidentally closed:

  1. Navigate to Live Game again
  2. A "Recover Game" prompt appears
  3. Click Recover to restore the last saved state

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Use a tablet for the best experience during games
  • Pre-load your playbook — tagged plays give you post-game effectiveness analysis
  • Set lineups before the game to save time during tracking
  • Check the +/- panel at halftime for substitution insights

docs.title: PDF Exports
docs.text: Generate professional, publication-ready PDF reports for games, players, teams, lineups, and seasons.

docs.title: From the Web Interface
docs.text:
Every game, player, and team page has a Export PDF button (usually top right of the page):

  1. Navigate to the specific game, player, or team page
  2. Click the Export PDF or Download Report button
  3. The PDF generates on-the-fly and downloads to your device

docs.title: Via Direct URL
docs.text:
Reports are accessible at their direct URLs (requires authentication):

https://your-app.com/reports/games/42/visual.pdf
https://your-app.com/reports/player/John%20Smith/scouting.pdf
https://your-app.com/reports/team/report.pdf

docs.title: Bulk Download
docs.text: The Download All button on the analytics dashboard generates a ZIP bundle containing: - Team report - Individual player PDFs for all active players - Aggregated statistics

docs.title: Visual Game Report
docs.text:
The most comprehensive game report includes:

  • Score Worm — Lead changes visualized throughout the game
  • Quarterly Scoring — Per-quarter points breakdown (bar chart)
  • Four Factors Dashboard — EFG%, TOV%, OREB%, FTA Rate
  • Top Performers — Leading scorers, rebounders, playmakers
  • Team Totals — Aggregated team statistics
  • Advanced Metrics — TS%, eFG%, Game Score, Net Rating

docs.title: Player Scouting Card
docs.text:
A compact one-page player profile:

  • Primary Stats — PPG, RPG, APG, FG%, 3P%, FT%
  • Advanced Metrics — USG%, PPS, TS%, eFG%, Game Score
  • Shot Quality Analysis — Expected vs actual points by zone
  • Zone Efficiency — Hot zone heatmap with color coding
  • Consistency Index — Coefficient of variation across games

docs.title: Game Summary
docs.text:
Standard box score format:

  • Player-by-player stat line (MIN, PTS, REB, AST, STL, BLK, TOV, PF)
  • Team totals
  • Shooting percentages by player
    • / - column

docs.title: Season Trend Report
docs.text:
Longitudinal analysis:

  • Rolling Averages — 5-game and 10-game rolling windows
  • Consistency Index — Coefficient of variation for key metrics
  • Performance Variance — Visualization of highs and lows

docs.title: Clutch Time Report
docs.text:
Pressure situation analysis:

  • Crunch Time — Score within 5 points, under 5 minutes remaining
  • Top Clutch Performers — Ranked by clutch points and efficiency
  • Team Clutch Summary — Aggregate clutch performance
  • Complete Clutch Table — All players with clutch stats

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution PDF is empty Ensure the game/player has data. A game with 0 shots cannot generate meaningful charts. Generation failed Check application logs. Common issues: missing font definitions, database timeouts. PDF won't download Check browser pop-up blocker settings. Try right-clicking the Export button and "Save Link As". Slow generation Large games with 50+ shot events may take 2–3 seconds. Reports are cached for 5 minutes. Missing reports Some report types require specific data (e.g., Clutch Report needs close-game data).

docs.title: Technical Details
docs.text:
• Engines: ReportLab (structured reports) + WeasyPrint (visual reports)
  • Generation: In-memory — no temporary files on disk
  • Graphics: Vector-based for crisp printing at any resolution
  • Caching: Reports cached for 5 minutes (configurable via CACHE_TIMEOUT)
  • Styles: Custom stylesheets ensure consistent branding across all reports

docs.title: Plays Management
docs.text: The Plays module lets you manage your team's digital playbook and associate plays with game events for post-game effectiveness analysis.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The system comes pre-loaded with 65+ plays covering standard offensive, defensive, and special situations:

Category Count Examples Offense 20+ Pick & Roll, Spain PNR, Horns Twist, UCLA Cut, Triangle Defense 20+ Man-to-Man, 2-3 Zone, 1-3-1 Zone, Box-and-One, Presses Special 25+ BLOB, SLOB, ATO, Game Winner, Quick Clock

docs.title: Viewing the Playbook
docs.text:
1. Click Plays in the sidebar navigation
  2. Use the filter buttons (All, Offense, Defense, Special) to narrow the view
  3. Click any play card to view full details and diagram

Play cards display: - Play name and description - Type badge (Offense/Defense/Special) - Difficulty rating - Tagged effectiveness (if used in games)

docs.title: Via Web Form
docs.text:
1. On the Plays page, click Add New Play
  2. Name — Enter a unique name for the play
  3. Type — Select the category (Offense/Defense/Special)
  4. Description — Detailed explanation of execution
  5. Diagram — Upload an image (PNG, JPG) of the play diagram

docs.title: Via Play Builder (Canvas)
docs.text:
1. Click Play Builder to open the full-screen drawing canvas
  2. Use the toolbar to create your play diagram:
    • Player Tokens — Drag player markers onto the court
    • Arrows — Draw movement paths (pass, cut, dribble, screen, shot, handoff)
    • Shapes — Add cones, boxes, and zone markers
    • Text — Label positions and actions
  3. Build animation sequences to show movement over time
  4. Save — the play is added to your playbook

docs.title: Play Builder Tools
docs.text:
The Play Builder is a Fabric.js-powered canvas with these tools:

Tool Icon Purpose Select ↖️ Move, resize, and edit elements Player ⭕ Add player tokens (numbered 1–5) Pass ➡️ Draw pass lines (dashed) Cut ➡️ Draw cut movement (solid) Dribble 〰️ Draw dribble path (zigzag) Screen 🛡️ Draw screen position Shot 🎯 Mark shot location Handoff ↔️ Draw handoff action Shape ⬜ Add cones, boxes, zones Text T Add labels and annotations

Animations: Use the timeline at the bottom to create frame-by-frame sequences showing how the play develops over time. Each frame saves the position of all elements.

docs.title: Edit
docs.text:
Update descriptions, diagrams, or canvas data as your playbook evolves:

  1. Navigate to the play detail page
  2. Click Edit to modify metadata or Edit in Builder to update the canvas diagram

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
Remove plays that are no longer used:

Historical Data

Deleting a play may affect historical stats if that play was tagged in past games. Associated shot events will lose their play reference.

docs.title: Tagging During Live Tracking
docs.text:
When recording a shot during live game tracking:

  1. After marking the shot location, the play selector appears
  2. Choose the associated play from your playbook
  3. The system links the shot event to the play for analysis

docs.title: Post-Game Analysis
docs.text:
After tagging plays in games, the system tracks:

Metric Description Frequency How often a play is run (total attempts) Efficiency Points Per Possession (PPP) for each play FG% Field goal percentage when running the play Shot Distribution Where shots come from when running the play

docs.title: Play Rankings
docs.text:
The analytics dashboard ranks plays by effectiveness:

Plays → Advanced Analytics → Plays Rankings

This shows which plays yield the highest points per possession against specific opponents or in specific situations.
